key_insight: General-purpose and foundation models were benchmarked against dermatology-specific classifiers to test how well they handle real-world skin lesion classification across different data sources and patient groups.
clinical_relevance: The study helps identify which AI approaches may be more reliable for clinical dermatology, especially when images come from varied devices, settings, and demographics.
method: Compared generalist vision, medical vision-language, and foundation models with task-specific dermatology classifiers.
Evaluated performance on recent dermatology datasets using dermoscopic images and smartphone clinical photos.
Tested robustness under distribution shift, modality change, and demographic variability.
evidence_signal: The abstract indicates a systematic benchmark on heterogeneous dermatology datasets, explicitly assessing generalization across modalities, devices, and demographic differences.
watch_item: Strong benchmark results may not directly translate to safe clinical deployment without external validation, calibration, and careful evaluation in local practice settings.
paper_title: Bridging Research and Practice: A Systematic Evaluation of Generalist and Dermatology-Specific Models in Clinical Skin Lesion Classification
